Rape cases registered in the country 
*244. DR. GYAN PRAKASH PILANIA: Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of rape cases registered in India, during 2004, with State-
wise break-up; 
(b) the number of rapes per lac of population in India, with State-wise break-
up; 
(c) in the light of above statistics, which were the first five States, where rape 
scenario was most alarming; and 
(d) the steps Government intend to take to improve the situation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI 
MANIKRAO GAVIT): (a) to (d) The total number of rape cases registered in India 
during 2004 and the number of rapes per lac of population, with State-wise breakup, is 
enclosed at Statement (See below) 
On the basis of rape cases registered, the five States with highest incidence of 
rape during 2004 were Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and 
Assam, while on the basis of the crime rate, the top five States during 2004 were 
Mizoram, Tripura, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Assam. 
'Public Order* and 'Police' as per the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of 
India are State subjects and, as such, registration, investigation, detection and 
prevention of crime is primarily the responsibility of the State Governments. 
Further, the Government of India has been from time to time issuing advisories 
to the State 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2005] 
Governments to make concerted efforts to improve the administration of the criminal 
justice system and to take effective measures to control crimes against vulnerable 
sections including women and children. In an advisory sent to the State Governments in 
May, 2004, the following points have been re-emphasized: 
i. There should be no delay in registration of FIR in cases of crime against 
women. 
ii. Cases should be thoroughly investigated and charge-sheets filed within three 
months from the date of occurrence of crime, 
iii. Police officials charged with the responsibility of protecting women 
should be sensitized adequately, 
iv. Helpline numbers of the Crime Against Women cells should be exhibited 
prominently in hospitals/schools/colleges premises, and in other suitable 
places. 
v. Women Police Cells and exclusive women police stations may also be set up 
to cater especially to women, as needed. 
vi. Women police officials should be recruited widely in the State Police Force. 
vii. Institutional support should be provided to victims of violence, and 
viii. Proper counselling should be provided to victims of rape.

*249. SHRI DHARAM PAL SABHARWAL: Will, the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that despite Supreme Court direction to N.D.M.C. to 
improve the parking facilities in Lutyen's Delhi, the N.D.M.C. has failed miserably to 
improve the construction of spacious Palika Parking at Connaught Place and has not

(b) if so, the reasons for this inordinate delay; and

commenced and completed?

directions to the New Delhi Municipal Council to improve the parking facility in 
Lutyen's Delhi. One multi-level parking constructed by New Delhi Municipal Council

allotted three sites to the New Delhi Municipal Council at Baba Kharak Singh Marg,

for construction of multi-level car parkings. New Delhi Municipal Council has decided to 
construct multi-level car parkings on the allotted sites on the Build, Own and transfer 
(BOT) basis as per the present schedule: 
(i) Commencement of tender process  — August, 2005 
(ii) Commencement of work on the project— 2006. 
(iii) Completion of the project— by the end of year 2008.

(d) if so, the action plan of Government to address these issues? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI P.M. SAYEED): (a) and (b) The energy 
deficit in April, 2005 varied from 7% to 25% in the States like J&K and Uttar Pradesh in 
Northern Region; Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra in Western Region; Bihar in 
Eastern; Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura in North Eastern 
Region. State-wise power supply position in the country for the month of April, 2005 
is given in the Statement. (See below). 
The supply and distribution of electricity to the ultimate consumers including 
domestic/industrial and farmers in a State is the responsibility of the concerned State  
Government/State Power Utility/Distribution 
147 

RAJYA SABHA [10 August, 2005] 
Agency. There is an overall shortage of power in the country which varies from State to 
State. In order to optimize utilisation of available power, power cuts/restrictions and 
load shedding are imposed by State Governments/State Power Utilities/Distribution 
Agencies from time to time so that the requirement of agricultural sector, supply to 
essential consumers and minimum requirement of core sector industries are 
adequately met. 
(c) and (d) There are a number of reasons for shortage of power including 
growth in demand for power outstripping the growth in generation and capacity 
addition, shortage of peaking power, low Plant Load Factor of thermal generating 
units mainly in the State sector, inadequate sub-transmission and distribution network 
in some States, high Transmission and Distribution losses, theft of power, poor financial 
position of States/Utilities rendering it difficult for them to raise the resources 
necessary for making required investments to create adequate additional generation, 
transmission and distribution capacity, etc. Theft of electricity causes commercial loss to 
the States/Power Utilities whereas leakage and losses in transmission and distribution 
system reduce the availability of power. 
The following measures have been taken/are proposed to be taken to address the issue 
of theft, leakage, transmission and commercial losses: 
(i) The Electricity Act, 2003 has been enacted and implemented with effect from 
10th June, 2003 under which the provisions relating to theft are made 
more stringent. 
(ii)     Compounding of theft cases. 
(iii)     Adoption of High Voltage Di stribution System (HVDS) in theft prone 
areas and rural areas. 
(iv)     Replacement of defective meters and installation of meters for all 
consumers. 
(v)     Replacement of LT overhead lines by insulated aerial bunched conductors

growth rates of these categories of products during January - March 2005 over

depending on the category. Thus the growth rate has been severely restricted in order 
to give a period of adjustment for the EU textile industry to adjust after the 
elimination of the quota system. This agreement will expire in 2007. India is a
